html:
The Tairona were a people of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the steep mountains on the Caribbean coast of northern Colombia, who built stone towns there before the Spanish conquest. Their culture was at its height from about 1000 to 1600.

They spoke a Chibchan language, related to that of the Muisca. They cut terraces into the slopes for maize and cassava, linked hundreds of villages with stone stairways and paths, and built towns such as Ciudad Perdida. Their goldsmiths cast fine pendants of gold and copper alloy, often of bat-men and birds.

The Spanish founded Santa Marta in 1525. The Tairona resisted for decades until the Spanish crushed a last revolt around 1600. Survivors withdrew higher up. The Kogi, Arhuaco, Wiwa and Kankuamo of the Sierra today see themselves as their heirs.
